subject: RFI: Inference deployment boundary brief and egress proof packet
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@edgesecure.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Deployment boundary, egress & threat compact packet

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this — our procurement and security teams are trying to close the RFI for our inference vendor shortlist. We need a concise package that covers:
- Network/topology diagram showing tenant/data/control plane demarcation
- Short isolation model description (how tenants are prevented from cross-talk)
- Egress controls: allowlist approach, IPs (or ephemeral ranges), and expected telemetry endpoints
- Key management summary (KMS/HSM, who holds keys, rotation cadence)
- One-paragraph threat summary and most-likely mitigations for lateral/egress risks

If possible, can you keep it to a single PDF plus a CSV of any public egress IPs? Our team prefers compact artifacts for the security review. Target: turnaround by EOD Monday PST.

Also include any HubSpot or evidence links we can attach to the procurement packet.

Best,
Priya
Procurement & Security Operations
EdgeSecure Ltd.

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@edgesecure.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Deployment boundary, egress & threat compact packet

Hi Priya — thanks, we can do a compact packet. I’ve pulled together a short PDF that contains:

- One-page topology diagram (control plane, data plane, tenant routing, egress gateways)
- Isolation model (per-tenant compute pools, strict SGs, and process-level namespace separation)
- Egress strategy (per-tenant ephemeral NAT IPs, egress allowlist only to our telemetry, KMS, and optional customer VPC peering targets)
- KMS / HSM flow (customer keys in their KMS when on Private; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed wrapping; rotation and audits noted)
- Threat synopsis (most realistic: compromised customer credentials or misconfigured peering; mitigations: least privilege, per-request provenance headers, per-tenant circuit breakers, and automated traffic anomaly detection)

Attached: redwood_inference_deployment_boundary_v1.pdf (compact packet), egress-iplist-ephemeral.csv (ephemeral NAT addresses we publish for allowlisting), kms-hsm-keyflow-diagram.png.

Short clarifications up front:
- For hosted customers we provide dedicated logical tenancy with strict network ACLs; we do not expose tenant-to-tenant internal IPs.
- We do maintain a small set of egress endpoints for core services (KMS, telemetry, model catalog); the CSV lists stable NAT ranges used for those endpoints. For high-security customers we support VPC peering or private link to eliminate public egress.
- Logs and audit events are retained per the contract; full audit artifacts can be provided in the evidence bundle on request.

Kimberly is on the thread for deeper security/diagram questions; Marissa is the infra owner who can supply any additional telemetry screenshots.

I’ll follow up Monday with any clarifications you need.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya@edgesecure.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgesecure.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Deployment boundary, egress & threat compact packet

Logan — received the packet, thank you. A couple quick follow-ups from security:
1) For the CSV you sent, can you confirm the publish cadence and how often those ephemeral NATs rotate? We need guidance for our allowlist maintenance windows.
2) For KMS: in the hosted model, when you say "Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed wrapping", do you continue to have key-encrypting-key access to ciphertext (i.e., can Redwood decrypt customer model artifacts), or is key escrow locked to a separate security boundary?
3) Can you provide the per-tenant telemetry collection endpoints (FQDNs) — our egress policy requires hostnames for TLS inspection rules.

Finally, our legal needs a short statement on SLA exceptions for egress-based failures (e.g., if one of Redwood's egress gateways is compromised) — a 2–3 sentence risk allocation note would be sufficient.

Thanks again,
Priya

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Deployment boundary, egress & threat compact packet

Priya — answers inline and a short legal-friendly blurb below. I’ve also attached an updated CSV with rotation cadence indicated.

1) NAT rotation cadence: our publicly announced ephemeral NAT ranges rotate on a 30–90 day schedule depending on capacity churn; for procurement allowlisting we recommend allowing the listed ranges and enabling a short exception process we coordinate via the support SLA for scheduled updates. The attached CSV now includes a "rotation_window_days" column.

2) KMS / ciphertext access: hosted customers who choose the Redwood-managed KMS model do not have their plaintext keys held by Redwood; we use HSM-wrapped keys and we do not permanently retain unencrypted customer key material. Decryption of customer model artifacts requires key access that is subject to RBAC, auditing, and customer-facing key policy constraints. For customers requiring cryptographic separation, our Private deployment model supports customer-managed KMS where Redwood never has access to the key-encrypting-key.

3) Telemetry endpoints: per-tenant telemetry is sent to telemetry.redwood-inference.com (TLS 1.3, mutual auth optional for Dedicated/Private). The updated attachment lists FQDNs for telemetry, model catalog, and KMS endpoints.

Risk allocation blurb for legal (2 sentences): 
"Redwood maintains layered egress controls and monitors for anomalous outbound traffic; in the event of an egress gateway compromise Redwood will notify affected customers per the agreed incident response SLA and will provide remediation and post-incident evidence. Customers requiring absolute physical separation should select a Private deployment or enable VPC peering; procurement of hosted services assumes shared control-plane infrastructure and associated residual risk."

If you want, Kimberly can provide a short diagram call to walk the team through the packet. Let us know a time.

Best regards,
Logan
